# Architecture

How the system is built: main parts, data flow, key design choices, and where code lives.

## Files

- [agent.md](agent.md) — **Agent — the loop, its model client, tools, citations and compaction (as built)**: The agent as built (agent/, llm/client.py GeminiChat, prompts/) - one Agent object per question with a prompt of [system, question, *history]; the code-side first search (the question searched as asked, before step 1); steps with a budget note; the stop rule in agent.md and the limits that force a finish (10 steps, 25 tool calls, a 30 s reserve, a failed call, two replies without a tool call); fallback and AgentError; the deadline chain from the server; compaction into a working memory (skipped, not replaced, when the call fails); the ToolBox (errors as text, ToolInputError messages) and finish; D#/R# citations resolved by code and handles in the answer text named by code; GeminiChat (raw turns re-sent, stand-in thought signature, limiter, ledger, retries, thinking level HIGH); settings; tracing; how the smoke, tune and held-out evals shaped it and why; known limits; tests. Read before changing the agent loop, its prompts, its limits, the chat client or the thinking setting. The tools themselves are corpus-tools.md.
- [corpus-tools.md](corpus-tools.md) — **Corpus tools — the agent's search, filter, field, key and read tools (as built)**: The seven deterministic tools the agent calls over the index, as built - search (scoped hybrid BM25 + dense, RRF, pages of 8 that search deeper, 2 passages of ~300 chars, exact phrases and keys), filter (any field, AND of eq/in/range/present/missing/contains, values resolved exact then loose, exact count, R# of every match), field_values, list_fields, read_fields, read_document, lookup_key; the rules they share (pages with exact totals and next offsets, nothing cut, D#/R# handles, ToolInputError messages, each date judged on its own), the field catalog in the system prompt, citations (R# expands to every id), the store reads behind them, tracing, measured times, known gaps and tests. Read before changing a tool, retrieval/, the tool texts or tools.json, or the store reads they use. The loop that calls them is agent.md.
- [dev-harness.md](dev-harness.md) — **Dev harness - rules, hooks, commands, checks and the eval split guard (as built)**: The setup for the coding agents (Claude Code and Codex) as built - the rule files (AGENTS.md imported by CLAUDE.md, with the split rule between markers; the global ~/.agent-harness rules and guard), the one command table (commands.json run as `uv run <key>` by src/corpusqa/devtasks.py; `check` and `precommit` composite keys), the project hooks in scripts/hooks/ shared by .claude/settings.json and .codex/hooks.json (split_reminder, guard_paths, guard_split, format_python, tests_on_stop), the permission deny rules and .ignore, the git pre-commit in .githooks/, the checks (ruff, pyright, import-linter's 5 contracts, offline tests, secret scan), the eval split files and their guards (scripts/make_eval_split.py, eval/sets/, questions-tune, the hashed no-hardcoding test), the project skills in docs/skills/, the tests of all this, and known limits. Read before changing a hook, a command key, a check, or anything about how the eval split is enforced.
- [eval.md](eval.md) — **Eval tooling — how the /ask question eval works**: The end-to-end question eval as built (eval/run.py, eval/ask_metrics.py, eval/questions.py; keys eval-smoke, eval-tune, eval-heldout, eval-all): its inputs (a running server, a question set, CLI options with defaults in config.py), the flow (one /health check, POST /ask per question with a semaphore and a per-question limit, contract checks, set-based scoring of the ids by group, then the answer judge), its outputs (summary.md, summary.json, per_question.jsonl, judge.jsonl, and where protected runs put them), the eval/history.csv row it adds (with a real example), its trace, and what is not built yet. Also the answer judge (eval/judge.py, prompt judge.md v1, gemini-3.1-pro-preview, fact by fact against answer_facts, two judgments per answer) and its calibration (eval/judge_calibrate.py, key eval-judge-calibrate; 99.3% fact agreement, kappa 0.90 on 150 hand-checked tune answers). Read before changing the eval runner, the judge, its report, its history row or the eval keys. The retrieval-only eval is in ../decisions/retrieval.md.
- [http-server.md](http-server.md) — **HTTP server (FastAPI) — how /health and /ask work**: The contract-facing HTTP layer as built: ./serve, config from env, the FastAPI app factory, background start-up with /health 503 → 200, the answerer factory that builds the agent once the Runtime is ready (no key - UnavailableAnswerer, the internal-error answer), the always-200 /ask path (own body parsing, AskQueue with 4 answers at once and the rest waiting, a deadline counted from arrival with asyncio.timeout_at, id filtering, size caps; the body is only answer and document_ids, the trace id goes in the X-Trace-Id response header), and the seams (Answerer, StartupFn → Runtime). Read before touching src/corpusqa/server/, config.py or ./serve.
- [ingestion.md](ingestion.md) — **Ingestion pipeline — how start-up builds the index (as built)**: The ingestion pipeline as built on ingest/build: S1–S10 in their real order (S4_date_window after S7, S6 after S8, S9 after the S10 publish), S6 chunk headers with learned field values, the index cache and its fingerprint, pruning, the embedding cache and spend ledger, what the Runtime holds, start-up flow and measured times, failure behaviour, tracing spans, where the build differs from the design, and what the agent's tools read (dates judged one by one against the learned window, person_norm in store/norms.py, CorpusReader). Read before touching src/corpusqa/ingest/, store/ or llm/, or before using the Runtime.
- [tracing.md](tracing.md) — **Tracing (Langfuse) — how corpusqa.obs works**: The tracing layer: obs facade with three backends (no-op, Langfuse, recording for tests), how /ask, the agent (agent, first_search, step, chat, tool, compact, citations, answer_handles) and start-up are traced, how to trace new code (trace, span, generation, observe), the safety rules (off without keys, never breaks a request, secrets scrubbed, bounded flush), the dev setup against Langfuse Cloud US (verified live 2026-10-16) and how to read a trace back through the v2 Observations API. Read before adding an LLM call, a tool or a pipeline stage, or when looking up a trace.
